consequence.statement: Karpenter no longer applies the karpenter.sh/managed-by annotation and instead adds an eks:eks-cluster-name tag, so the identifying metadata on affected resources differs from previous releases; anything matching the old annotation will no longer find it.
consequence.remediation: Verify whether any tooling, selectors or automation read the karpenter.sh/managed-by annotation or should consume the new eks:eks-cluster-name tag.

original.statement: Karpenter v1.0.0 removes the karpenter.sh/managed-by annotation and adds an eks:eks-cluster-name tag instead.

decision.reason: [ev-6d7e63820de1] and the linked PR [ev-e34f0f43f7ac] say that karpenter.sh/managed-by is dropped because it was "an artifact of a migration path and not something needed in the future", and that eks:eks-cluster-name is added to support pod identity sessions. Neither source says that anything fails, is rejected or stops being honoured. Because the metadata only differs from earlier releases, low-severity behavior-change in the review class is the strongest supported consequence, and it does not over-claim mandatory work. Confidence is low because the evidence does not name which resources carry the annotation or tag, or what depends on them.
